Consonantal i

Theme

Latin word

pictūra

pictūra, pictūrae f.

noun, first declension

a picture or pattern, painted, woven or embroidered; picture, painting

In this lexicon

  • design

    the recommended word · classical · Lucr. 2.35: textilibus pictūrīs (Lewis & Short); Cic. Verr. 2.4.1 (Lewis & Short)

  • picture

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Verr. 2.4.1; Sen. Ep. 16.8; Traupman 360

Notes

  1. 1pictūra: short i (Traupman 360 pīctūra). Lewis & Short leaves the vowel unmarked, as in pictus and pictor; de Vaan 465 sets Proto-Italic *pikto-, painted. The libellī write pictūrās.

Examples

  • Theodōrus librum ā patre accēpit, et ōre clausō, oculīs apertīs, pictūrās spectāvit.

    Theo took the book from Dad and, with his mouth shut and his eyes open, looked at the pictures.Libellus VI, Reditus: per Alpēs domum

    In the entry for picture

  • animum pictūrā pāscit inānī

    he feeds his heart on the empty pictureVerg. A. 1.464

    In the entry for picture

  • rērumque ignārus imāgine gaudet

    and, knowing nothing of what it shows, he delights in the pictureVerg. A. 8.730
